help_sub.message: Common questions and key behaviors. Click an item to expand.

help_1_body.message:
Firefox has a built-in "Bookmarks menu" location (starred addresses are saved there by default). Chrome has no equivalent, so the extension creates a same-named folder under Chrome's bookmarks bar to hold them.

In Chrome, deleting this "Bookmarks menu" folder only clears the bookmarks inside it (synced to all devices); the folder itself is restored automatically — by design, not a bug. Please don't delete it repeatedly; to empty the menu, delete the bookmarks inside instead.

help_2_body.message: All bookmark operations are encrypted on your device before upload (AES-256-GCM); the server only stores ciphertext. On first use you set a sync passphrase; on a new device or after reinstalling, sign in and enter the same passphrase to sync. The passphrase itself is never uploaded — only a decryption key derived from it, on your device. Forgot the passphrase = data unrecoverable, so save it in a password manager.

help_3_body.message: Deleting a bookmark or folder creates a "tombstone" synced to all devices — deletes are consistent everywhere and deleted items won't be pulled back from the cloud. Deleting the "Bookmarks menu" folder is the exception: only its contents are cleared, the folder stays.

help_4_body.message:
1. Remember your sync passphrase on the old device;
2. On the new device, install the extension and sign in to the same account;
3. Enter the same passphrase when prompted;
4. Click "Sync now" and your bookmarks are restored from the cloud. A default sync space is created automatically — no need to make one.

help_5_body.message: Extensions loaded via developer mode don't auto-update: after changing code, rebuild (npm run build) and click "Reload" on the browser's extension management page.

help_6_body.message: Each space is an independent bookmark tree (e.g. work / personal) that can bind to a different browser profile; Free includes 1 space, Plus 3, Pro / Lifetime 10. Synced browsers register automatically — view, rename or unlink them here.

help_7_title.message: 📡 How to read the sync-complete message?

help_7_body.message:
Sync messages describe the direction of the result; they no longer show "pushed/pulled N" — that number counts internal sync operations, which never matches your actual bookmark count. Reference:

MessageMeaning
First sync complete — bookmarks uploaded encryptedThis device uploaded its bookmarks to the cloud for the first time (the cloud was empty)
First sync complete — bookmarks restored from the cloudNew device or reinstall pulled existing cloud bookmarks
Two-way sync completeBoth this device and others had changes; both directions synced
Uploaded local changesOnly local new/changed bookmarks were uploaded
Synced changes from other devicesReceived new bookmarks added by other devices
Already up to dateNo changes, nothing to do
⚠️ N local bookmarks not shown hereThe space has device-local bookmarks, but this Chrome has no local Bookmarks bar to hold them — when signed in with an empty local tree, Chrome doesn't create one

The "N bookmarks" on the status card is the true total and is accurate. "⚠️ N cloud entries failed to decrypt" means your sync key doesn't match the cloud data — check your key or passphrase.

To show them on this device: sign out of Chrome, then create one local bookmark (when signed out, only the local Bookmarks bar exists). Once it appears, sync again. They stay on this device and are never uploaded to your Google account.
